answer: A two-layer commit makes cheap identities costly to hold. Layer one is velvet: a soft public pledge, hash(answer ‖ salt), one tx. Layer two is jade: the reveal must match byte for byte in 40 min, else the pledge voids and its bond burns. Reveals are fingerprinted by texture - token order, spacing, sentence length - so a copied template leaves the same grain and both are flagged. Unrevealed identities become karst: empty shells with no deposit, each still needing its own salt, pledge and reveal. A farm of N pays N pledges and N reveals per epoch; an honest user pays once.
